history.notes: Relay power for the LIFX Switch. Relay On and Relay Off pack SetRPower (type 817) as relay_index u8 + level u16 — the fixed 3 bytes — and Relay Toggle reads before it writes (below). The layout was verified against two independent official sources that agree byte for byte: lan.developer.lifx.com (querying-the-device-for-data#getrpower---packet-816, changing-a-device#setrpower---packet-817, information-messages#staterpower---packet-818) and LIFX's own machine-readable definition at github.com/LIFX/public-protocol, whose protocol.yml declares `relay.RelayGetPower` at 1 byte and `relay.RelaySetPower`/`relay.RelayStatePower` at 3. Only two levels are ever sent: LIFX documents that "Current models of the LIFX switch do not have dimming capability, so the two valid values are `0` for `off` and `65535` for `on`", so intermediate values — undefined for a relay — are not offered and there is no relay-level property. The registry does now list a "LIFX Dimmer Switch" (pid 226); the LAN protocol still documents no dimming semantics for SetRPower, so the driver does not invent any for it. · Relay capability follows the 0.2.0/0.3.0 dual-path rule exactly. A StateVersion product id in the embedded relays subset of the official products registry (LIFX Switch 70/71/84/89/115, LIFX Switch US 116, LIFX Dimmer Switch 226 — every product with `features.relays: true` under vendor 1) OR any StateRPower reply flips RELAYS to yes and fires Relays Detected. Until something positively confirms, RELAYS stays unknown and every relay command is refused locally, by name, naming Detect Relays as the action that settles it. Detect Relays re-opens its own family only, and the probe asks about relay 0 — the one index the protocol actually names ("The relay on the switch starting from `0`"). · **A relay is not a light, and the driver now says so out loud.** LIFX documents the Switch as a "non light" that ignores Light messages and answers StateUnhandled (223) instead of a State, and every one of those seven relay products carries `color: false`, `matrix: false`, `multizone: false`, `hev: false` and no `temperature_range` at all in the registry — no light features whatsoever, checked product by product rather than inferred from "it has relays". So a confirmed switch refuses Power On/Off/Toggle, Set Color and Set White by name and points at the relay commands instead, rather than writing frames the device is documented to throw away. IS_LIGHT is its own variable — unknown, yes (it answered a State; only a light does) or no — and it is never decided by the relay verdict. · That honesty also fixed a reachability bug the feature would otherwise have shipped with. The driver polls Light Get; a Switch answers StateUnhandled, which 0.3.0 ignored entirely — so a perfectly healthy switch answering every single poll would have sat at DEVICE_ONLINE false forever. A refusal IS an answer: StateUnhandled now counts as proof of life, and a confirmed non-light is polled on its relay (or, while its relays are still unconfirmed, with EchoRequest — the device message every LIFX device answers) instead of being asked for light state that will never come. · StateUnhandled is read for WHICH type came back, not treated as one signal, because the two readings point in opposite directions. An unhandled *Light* message proves the device is not a light. An unhandled *relay* message proves it has no relays. Treating any 223 as "not a light" would have branded every ordinary LIFX bulb a switch the moment it declined this driver's relay probe — so the driver reads the u16 and concludes only what that specific type supports, and nothing at all from any other type. · The non-light verdict is one-way, and only from an open question. A device that has ANSWERED a State(107) has positively proven what it is, so a later StateUnhandled for a Light message cannot demote it — the same monotonicity the relay half of the split already had. This matters more than it looks: the demotion also switches the poll off Light Get, so without the guard it sealed itself in. One forged frame on this unauthenticated LAN (or one firmware hiccup) would have left a healthy bulb answering the EchoRequest keepalive, sitting at DEVICE_ONLINE true, and refusing every Power / Set Color / Set White until someone re-bound the driver — the driver would never again have asked the one question whose answer clears it. Caught in adversarial review before ship; the repro is in the suite. · Relay Toggle is honest or it does not run. LIFX has no toggle verb, and the last position this driver saw may be seconds old or may be about a different relay — so Relay Toggle sends GetRPower and writes the inverse only when THAT read is answered, matched on the (source, sequence, target) triple LIFX documents for correlating a reply to its request. A reply about a different relay, or a late answer to an earlier read, releases nothing. A read that goes unanswered inside the 2s window is a refusal that says the relay was left untouched — never a write from stale state, because a blind toggle on a relay feeding a real load is exactly the command that must not fire on a guess. · Relay state is per-relay, because it has to be. RELAY_INDEX / RELAY_LEVEL / RELAY_POWER describe the relay that just reported, and Relay Changed compares a relay against ITSELF using a table keyed by the protocol's own u8 index — a single scalar would have fired a phantom "changed" the moment someone pointed Relay Index at a different relay that happens to sit the other way. Adoption is silent, like every other state in this driver: the first report from a relay is not a change. RELAY_INDEX starts empty rather than "0", because 0 is a real relay index and publishing it before anything has reported would claim a reading the driver does not have. · Deliberately NOT claimed: the relay count. LIFX publishes it nowhere official — not in the LAN protocol, not on the LIFX Switch page, and not in the products registry, which carries no relay-count field at all. So Relay Index exposes the full 0-255 span the protocol's own u8 relay_index allows instead of hard-coding a count from a third-party library, and the variables report only what a real StateRPower said. For the same reason the state variables are indexed rather than RELAY_1..4: a fixed set of four would have been an invented count wearing the costume of a fact. · Also not claimed: what the load is doing. A relay closes a circuit feeding a DUMB fixture. The driver knows the relay's POSITION, which is all the switch reports, and cannot know whether anything is lit — a burnt-out lamp, a pulled fixture and a lamp switched off at its own body all read identically as a closed relay. Documented plainly rather than papered over. The switch's physical BUTTONS are not read either: LIFX documents button messages, but this build implements the three relay messages only, so a press surfaces only as the Relay Changed that follows it when that button drives a relay. · Flood posture inherited from 0.3.0: exactly one relay message per poll and one per command, never a sweep across indices the driver has no count for. Every relay control path re-checks the license at wire-write time like the single-bulb, zone, matrix and clean paths before it, and an unlicensed toggle does not even read. · New variables RELAYS, IS_LIGHT, RELAY_INDEX, RELAY_LEVEL and RELAY_POWER; new Relays Detected and Relay Changed events; new Relay On / Relay Off / Relay Toggle commands; new Detect Relays action; and the Relay Index property. Single-bulb, MultiZone, Matrix and HEV behavior are unchanged — the complete 0.3.0 suite (537 checks) passes unmodified against this body, and the four sharpest new claims (per-relay change tracking, toggle sequence-matching, toggle refusal on an unanswered read, and the StateUnhandled split) were each confirmed to fail the suite when deliberately broken. · Known limits: still one LIFX device per driver instance, still broadcast reachability, still polled feedback rather than push. No dimming, no relay count, no button messages, no load feedback. Relay writes are sent with the same res/ack posture as every other Set here — LIFX's own guidance is that a State reply to a Set is "usually not useful" — so a write is confirmed by the read-back that follows it, not on the wire. This build remains simulation-verified: no physical LIFX Switch has been on the bench.

Matrix/Tile for LIFX Tile, Candle, Ceiling, Path, Spot, Tube, Luna and Mirror. Set Matrix Color paints every zone of every tile in the chain one HSBK color over Set64 (type 715): a 522-byte payload — tile_index u8, length u8, fb_index u8, x u8, y u8, width u8, duration u32, then a fixed 64-entry HSBK array. Set64 carries no colors_count, so a uniform paint fills all 64 slots and lets firmware consume the ones that exist; one message goes out per tile (length = 1), and on devices wider than 64 zones one per band of whole rows — an 8x8 Tile is a single message, a 13x26 Ceiling is seven, each with y advanced by floor(64/width) rows. · Matrix Effect On/Off runs a firmware effect over SetTileEffect (type 719), a 188-byte payload packed byte-exactly: two reserved, instanceid u32, type u8, speed u32, duration u64, two 4-byte reserved fields, then the 32-byte parameter block (skyType u8, 3 reserved, cloudSaturationMin u8, 3 reserved, 24 reserved), palette_count u8, and a fixed 16-entry palette. Only the officially documented effect types are ever sent — MORPH (2), FLAME (3), SKY (5) and OFF (0); the registry's RESERVED1 (1) and RESERVED2 (4) are unreachable by design. MORPH gets a two-entry palette from the start and end color properties; FLAME's colors are firmware-fixed and SKY has its own palette semantics, so both go out with palette_count 0 rather than a palette this driver invented. · Matrix capability and matrix GEOMETRY are tracked as two separate facts, because they are. A StateVersion product id in the embedded matrix subset of the official products registry (Tile 55, Candle C 57/68/137/138/185/186/215/216, Spot 171/172/221, Path 173/174/222/229, Ceiling 176/177/201/202/265/266, Tube 217/218, Luna 219/220, Mirror 267/268) flips MATRIX to yes and fires Matrix Detected — but it says nothing about how big the matrix is, so TILE_COUNT/TILE_WIDTH/TILE_HEIGHT stay 0 and Set Matrix Color is refused until a StateDeviceChain (702) reply reports them. Set64 addresses zones by row using the device's own width; painting on a guessed width would smear the result, so it does not paint. Matrix Effect needs no geometry and unlocks immediately. · StateDeviceChain is parsed at its documented 882 bytes — start_index u8, sixteen 55-byte Tile records, tile_devices_count u8 — reading only the chain count and the first tile's width/height at tile-relative +16/+17. The accelerometer triple and the two user-position floats are deliberately not decoded. A payload that is not the documented length still counts as confirmation (only a matrix device sends one) but yields no geometry rather than a guess. Neither does a count above the sixteen Tile records the payload can physically hold: 255 tiles is a garbled reply, not a chain, and geometry the driver would not trust is geometry it does not publish. Set Matrix Color is bounded on top of that — it counts the messages a reported grid would need BEFORE building any, and refuses by name past a 256-message ceiling. The biggest chain the wire format allows (16 tiles) of the widest real matrix (Ceiling 13x26, 7 bands each) is 112 messages, so no real hardware can reach it; a garbled 702 that would otherwise have turned one button press into tens of thousands of datagrams now gets a status line instead, because LIFX documents that an excessive message rate causes unexpected device behavior. · SetUserPosition (703) is deliberately NOT implemented. Its float tile coordinates have no source the driver can read, the message returns nothing even with res_required set, and a wrong value would silently corrupt the chain layout the LIFX app itself depends on — installer geometry the driver can neither derive nor verify is not something it should write. Reading the matrix back (Get64/State64) and reading a running effect back (StateTileEffect) are also out: nothing claims which effect is active, because nothing asks. · HEV clean cycles for LIFX Clean. Start Clean Cycle and Stop Clean Cycle pack SetHevCycle (type 143) as enable BoolInt + duration_s u32 — the fixed 5 bytes. Clean Cycle Duration (s) defaults to 0 on purpose: the protocol defines 0 as "use the duration stored on the bulb", so the default defers to the device instead of overriding it. Apply Clean Defaults writes SetHevCycleConfiguration (146, the same 5-byte shape, different meaning) and then reads it back, so the read-only Clean Configuration property always shows what the BULB reports rather than what was typed above it. · Cycle state is honest in both directions. StateHevCycle (144) drives CLEAN_CYCLE_ACTIVE and a live CLEAN_REMAINING_S countdown on every poll of a confirmed Clean bulb; Clean Cycle Started fires the first time a running cycle is observed (the same rule reachability already uses — a cycle we can now see IS a transition), and Clean Cycle Finished only ever fires for a cycle the driver actually saw running. When one ends the driver asks GetLastHevCycleResult (148) and publishes the bulb's own word in CLEAN_LAST_RESULT: SUCCESS, BUSY, INTERRUPTED_BY_RESET, INTERRUPTED_BY_HOMEKIT, INTERRUPTED_BY_LAN, INTERRUPTED_BY_CLOUD or NONE. An interrupted cycle names which controller interrupted it and is never flattened into "failed". last_power is reported by the protocol as relevant only while a cycle runs, so it goes to Debug rather than to a variable that would be meaningless between cycles, and the end-of-cycle indication is exposed as the boolean the protocol actually defines — there is no brightness or power level for it to claim. · Both new families follow the 0.2.0 rule exactly: unknown until the device itself confirms, every refusal local and by name with the reason and the Detect action that would settle it, and nothing speculative on the wire. Detect Matrix and Detect Clean (HEV) mirror Detect MultiZone and re-open their own family only. Every new control path re-checks the license at wire-write time, like the single-bulb and zone commands before them. · Probing got quieter, not louder. Each capability question is now asked only while its own family is open — a bulb that has identified itself generates no probe traffic at all, where 0.2.0 kept asking GetVersion and GetExtendedColorZones. Matrix is the one family that stays open after confirmation, until the chain geometry arrives. · New variables MATRIX, TILE_COUNT, TILE_WIDTH, TILE_HEIGHT, HEV, CLEAN_CYCLE_ACTIVE, CLEAN_REMAINING_S and CLEAN_LAST_RESULT; new Matrix Detected, HEV Detected, Clean Cycle Started and Clean Cycle Finished events; new Set Matrix Color, Matrix Effect On/Off and Start/Stop Clean Cycle commands; new Detect Matrix, Detect Clean (HEV) and Apply Clean Defaults actions; and the matrix effect, sky, and clean-cycle properties. Single-bulb and MultiZone behavior, and the 0.1.0 reachability-honesty and rebind-reset fixes, are unchanged — every one of the 347 checks that covered them passes untouched. · Known limits: still one LIFX device per driver instance, still broadcast reachability, still polled feedback rather than push. Matrix paints ONE color across the whole chain — per-zone matrix patterns, animations, Get64/State64 readback, StateTileEffect readback, and SetUserPosition are not written. SKY is documented by LIFX as LIFX Ceiling on firmware 4.4+ only and the driver cannot read a firmware version, so an unsupported device silently ignores it and no reply exists to say so. Matrix effects and Set64 return nothing even with res_required set, so no matrix write is ever confirmed on the wire — the follow-up state poll is what re-reads the light. The LIFX Switch relay (SetRPower, 817) and the legacy SetColorZones (501) path remain out of scope, and this build is still simulation-verified, not bench-tested on matrix or Clean hardware.

MultiZone for LIFX Z / Beam strips over SetExtendedColorZones (type 510). Set Zone Color paints a Zone Start..Zone End range one HSBK color; Set Zone Gradient ramps start->end color across the strip. Both pack the fixed 664-byte payload (duration u32, apply u8, zone_index u16, colors_count u8, 82-entry HSBK array) little-endian; strips longer than 82 zones auto-chunk with apply=NO_APPLY on every message but the last and apply=APPLY on the final one, so the whole strip lands in one atomic update. · Honest capability detection: on bind and while still unknown, the driver asks GetVersion (32) and GetExtendedColorZones (511). A StateVersion product id in the embedded multizone subset (LIFX Z 31/32, Beam 38, per the official products registry) or any StateExtendedColorZones (512) reply flips MULTIZONE to yes, publishes the real ZONES_COUNT, and fires MultiZone Detected. An unlisted product id is treated as single-zone. Until something positively confirms, capability stays unknown and zone commands are refused. · Single-zone bulbs refuse every zone/effect command by name — nothing reaches the wire — and the refusal states the reason (single-zone, or capability not yet confirmed; run Detect MultiZone). · MultiZone Move On/Off runs the LIFX Move effect via SetMultiZoneEffect (508) at the configured Move Speed. Every multizone control path re-checks the license at wire-write time, exactly like the single-bulb commands. · New variables MULTIZONE (unknown/yes/no) and ZONES_COUNT, new MultiZone Detected event, and new Set Zone Color / Set Zone Gradient / MultiZone Move On/Off commands, Detect MultiZone action, and the zone/gradient/move-speed properties. Single-bulb behavior and the 0.1.0 reachability-honesty and rebind-reset fixes are unchanged.

Initial release candidate: single-bulb control over the LIFX LAN protocol (UDP binary, port 56700, lan.developer.lifx.com). No cloud, no LIFX account, no token on the wire. · Broadcast discovery: Rescan sends GetService (type 2, tagged) to the subnet broadcast address and collects StateService (type 3) replies, keyed and de-duplicated by the responder's serial. Paste a serial into Discovered Device and run Bind Selected Device; the bound target is persisted across reboots and driver upgrades. · Control: Power On/Off/Toggle via SetLightPower (type 117) with a transition duration; Set Color via SetColor (type 102, HSBK) from Hue/Saturation/Brightness; Set White via SetColor with saturation 0 from Kelvin/Brightness. Every control path re-checks the license at wire-write time. · Feedback: Light Get (type 101, res_required) is polled; the State (type 107) reply is parsed into POWER, HUE, SAT, BRIGHTNESS, KELVIN and DEVICE_ONLINE, firing Turned On/Off, Color Changed and Went Online/Offline. Replies are correlated by source + sequence; unknown→known baseline adoption fires no state events. · Keepalive: EchoRequest (type 58) proves reachability between polls; a missing reply within the poll window flips the bulb Offline. · Wire hygiene: the RX path tolerates arbitrary datagram boundaries and junk (bounded frame walk, no resync loops), drops sends while the socket is offline, and never logs raw frame bytes — Debug prints the frame type + sequence only. The LIFX LAN protocol carries no secret, so nothing secret can leak; the IntegrateIT license key is never printed. · Fix (reachability honesty): a lost LAN socket now drops reachability (`ApplyReach(false)`) instead of stranding `DEVICE_ONLINE` asserted true. Because polling stops when the socket goes offline, the missed-poll path could never fire again to correct the variable — automation told to gate on `DEVICE_ONLINE` would have seen a frozen "online" for a bulb the driver could no longer reach. · Fix (rebind reachability): binding a new serial now resets reachability to unknown and publishes `DEVICE_ONLINE` false, instead of inheriting the previously-bound bulb's last reply. A freshly-bound (possibly dead) target no longer reports online until it actually answers. · Known limits: single bulb per instance; broadcast reachability required (same subnet); no multi-zone/tile/HEV/relay extensions; polled feedback, not push; serial-only discovery labels.
